contribution.position: My position is unchanged. On reliability the evidence is still unfavorable. The perf report records cold_start at 1900ms at peak load against an 800ms budget, about 2.4x over. The 600ms figure cited on the risk axis does not appear in that artifact, so it either reflects non-peak conditions or is unsupported. The incident log shows two sev2 incidents last quarter, both traced to retry storms. A slow cold start at peak can plausibly feed that same failure mode. The test report (412 passed, 0 failed, 87% coverage) shows functional correctness but nothing about peak-load or retry behavior, so it does not offset the perf gap. The cost and operability points raised by the other roles are not reliability evidence. Rollback in runbook v4 lowers recovery cost but does not prevent the failure. What would move this axis: a peak-load test showing cold_start within 800ms or a documented waiver for the overage, plus evidence of retry and backoff behavior under peak load that rules out a repeat of the retry-storm incidents.
